1.title: Virtual Machines
1.text: Welcome to Module eight: Virtual Machines. It covers the exam area Deploy and manage Azure compute resources. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do six things. Create a virtual machine. Configure Azure Disk Encryption. Move a virtual machine to another resource group, subscription or region. Manage virtual machine sizes. Manage virtual machine disks. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: Deploy and manage Azure compute resources (twenty-twenty-five percent). Exam format: one hundred minutes; a score of seven hundred on a scale of one to one thousand passes. Validated against: the official Microsoft Learn A Z-one hundred four study guide, skills measured as of October twenty-six, two thousand twenty-three.

1.title: Creating a virtual machine
1.text: Creating a virtual machine. An Azure virtual machine is I A A S: you manage the guest operating system, Azure manages the host hardware. Subscription, resource group, name, region. Region decides latency, cost and available sizes. Image. Windows Server, Linux distributions, or a custom image. Size. C P U, memory, storage, network capacity. Authentication. Password or S S H key (Linux). Disks. O S disk, optional data disks. Networking. V net, subnet, public I P, N S G. Management. Boot diagnostics, managed identity, auto-shutdown, extensions.

1.title: Creating a virtual machine, continued
1.text: Creating a virtual machine. The figure shows this: Components of a V M: size, O S disk, data disks, network interface and the temporary disk.

1.title: Creating a virtual machine, continued
1.text: Creating a virtual machine. V M extensions run post-deployment tasks (install software, run scripts, configure). Stopped (deallocated) V Ms do not charge for compute, but disks still cost; a V M that is only stopped from inside the O S keeps billing for compute. Exam tip: To stop compute billing, stop the V M from the portal (state "Stopped (deallocated)").

1.title: Sizes
1.text: Sizes. B (burstable). Low baseline C P U, bursts: dev or test, small sites. D (general purpose). Balanced C P U and memory. E (memory optimized). Databases, in-memory. F (compute optimized). C P U-heavy workloads. N (G P U). Graphics and machine learning. Resizing changes the size: it may require a restart, and if the new size is not available on the current hardware cluster, you stop (deallocate) the V M first.

1.title: Disks
1.text: Disks. O S disk. Holds the operating system; persistent. Data disk. Additional persistent storage; attach, detach, resize. Temporary disk. Local to the host, for page and swap files; data is lost on redeploy or some maintenance. Managed disks. Azure manages the storage account; types: Standard H D D, Standard S S D, Premium S S D, Premium S S D version two, Ultra Disk. Increase a disk's size by deallocating the V M (for most cases), then resizing the disk; you cannot shrink a disk. Exam tip: Important data never goes on the temporary disk (drive D: on Windows).

1.title: Disk encryption
1.text: Disk encryption. Server-side encryption (S S E). Default for managed disks, with platform-managed keys (or customer-managed keys). Azure Disk Encryption (A D E). Bit Locker (Windows) or D M-Crypt (Linux) inside the V M; keys in Azure Key Vault; encrypts O S and data disks. Encryption at host. Encrypts temporary disks and caches at the host. A D E needs Azure Key Vault in the same region and subscription with the right access policy (enabled for disk encryption).

1.title: Moving a VM
1.text: Moving a V M. To another resource group or subscription. Move the V M and its related resources (disks, N I C, public I P) with the portal's Move action; the V M's location stays the same; the resource I D changes. To another region. Use Azure Resource Mover (or Site Recovery), or re-create from a template, disk copy or image. Exam tip: Stopped from inside the O S is not deallocated: compute billing continues until the V M is stopped in Azure.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. A team wants to stop paying for V M compute at night. What should they do? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Stop the V M from the Azure portal so it is deallocated. Deallocated V Ms do not incur compute charges.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. Where should a V M store application data that must survive a redeploy? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: A data disk. The temporary disk can lose data; data disks persist.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. An administrator wants Bit Locker encryption for a Windows V M with keys held in Key Vault. Which feature fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Azure Disk Encryption. A D E uses Bit Locker with keys in Key Vault.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. A V M must change to a larger size. What is true? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: It may need to be restarted, and sometimes deallocated first. Resizing can require a restart or deallocation.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. A team moves a V M to another subscription. What else should move with it? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Its disks, network interface and public I P. Related resources move together with the V M.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. Which V M size family suits memory-intensive databases? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: E (memory optimized). The E family has a high memory-to-C P U ratio.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. What does a deallocated V M stop charging for? Answer: Compute. Question two. Which disk loses data on redeploy? Answer: The temporary disk. Question three. What does Azure Disk Encryption use on Windows? Answer: Bit Locker, with keys in Azure Key Vault.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. Can you shrink a managed disk? Answer: No. Question five. Name two managed disk types. Answer: For example Standard S S D and Premium S S D. Question six. What runs post-deployment tasks on a V M? Answer: V M extensions.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Create: image, size, auth, disks, networking, extensions. Billing: deallocated equals no compute charge; disks still billed. Disks: O S, data, temporary (not persistent); managed types. Encryption: S S E default; A D E (Bit Locker or D M-Crypt, Key Vault); encryption at host. Move: resource group or subscription with related resources; region via Resource Mover.
